questions.prompt: Data {0, 2, 4} under N(2, 8/3) (the MLE). What is the average log-likelihood? (decimal, tolerance 0.002)
questions.explanation: σ²=8/3; each point's quadratic term averages to 1: −½[ln(2π·2.667)+1]=−1.909.

questions.prompt: The MLE variance (divisor n) of the data {2, 4, 6, 8}. (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
0.4·N(−1,1)+0.6·N(2,1), x=0. What is the responsibility of component 1? (decimal, tolerance 0.002)
In an M-step, responsibilities for points (1, 2, 6) are (0.5, 0.25, 0.25). What is the updated mean? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
After an EM iteration, the training log-likelihood goes down. What does that indicate?
options: The learning rate is too high for the M step
A bug (EM is guaranteed not to decrease the likelihood)
Normal EM behaviour, as the likelihood can oscillate
The model is overfitting the training data
questions.explanation: Each full E+M iteration cannot decrease the likelihood, so a decrease signals an implementation error.

questions.prompt: KL(N(μ=0, σ²=4) ‖ N(0,1)) = ½(σ²+μ²−1−ln σ²). Compute it. (decimal, tolerance 0.002)
questions.skillLabel: The ELBO and its KL term

questions.prompt: Which statement about the ELBO is correct?
options: It does not depend on the decoder p(x|z), only on the encoder
It upper-bounds log p(x); the gap is KL(p(z|x) ‖ q(z|x))
It equals log p(x) for any encoder q(z|x) that is normalised
It lower-bounds log p(x); the gap is KL(q(z|x) ‖ p(z|x))
questions.skillLabel: The ELBO and its KL term

questions.prompt: Training log-likelihoods −2.1 and held-out −2.5 for K=10; K=3 gives train −2.2 and held-out −2.25. By how many nats per point does K=3 beat K=10 on held-out data? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
A generator always outputs samples near one data mode. Which pair of measurements describes it?
options: Low gap fraction (realistic) but one mode with nearly all the sample proportion
High held-out likelihood, since the modes it covers are modelled well
Low reconstruction error, since a generator must reproduce the inputs
High gap fraction (unrealistic) and roughly uniform mode proportions
questions.explanation: Mode collapse yields realistic samples with almost no diversity.

questions.prompt: A generator's samples have mode proportions (0.7, 0.3, 0.0) while the true data weights are (0.3, 0.4, 0.3). What is the total variation distance ½Σ|p−q|? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
A mixture fit gives training log-likelihood +∞ for one run. Diagnose and fix.
rubric: A component's variance collapsed onto one point so its density diverges.
Fix: variance floor, a prior on the variance, fewer components or restarts.
Check: held-out likelihood should fall for that run, and the minimum variance should be monitored during EM.
